NOCTURNE

Case study: an online vinyl record store that reads like an independent music magazine and works as a full-featured shop.

Project type
Website, e-commerce
Role
UX/UI design, art direction, front-end
Tools
Figma, HTML, CSS, JavaScript
Year
2026
01

The brief

NOCTURNE sells vinyl to collectors and to people for whom music is culture, not background. The brief had two demands that usually pull in opposite directions: the mood of an independent magazine and the convenience of a real shop.

01

A recognisable look

No identical cards or stock blocks — the client had already rejected templated stores.

02

An easy catalogue

Filters, sorting, search and two ways to browse.

03

The full purchase path

Cart, favourites, checkout. There was no backend, so everything runs on local data.

02

Audience

WhoWhat they look forHow the interface answers
CollectorA specific pressing, disc and sleeve condition, yearTwo Goldmine grades with a scale, edition and catalogue number, a condition filter
Music lover, 18–40To discover something new and see why a record mattersCurated collections, editorial picks, “similar albums”
Mobile shopperTo find and buy quicklyBottom tab bar, filters in a sheet, sticky buy button
03

Idea

Magazine × shop

The site is laid out like a magazine issue: the home page has an issue number and date, sections are numbered, texts use drop caps and pull quotes. Underneath sits strict shop mechanics: price, stock and the buy button are always in the same place.

01

Editorial

Big grotesque with italic serif, asymmetric grids, type over images.

02

Analogue

The record runs through everything: it slides out, spins and becomes the page curtain.

03

Function

Filters live in the URL; every state — empty, sold out, error — is designed.

LP · 1962 · NM / VG+

36 covers drawn by code

There were no photos, and stock images would have made it look templated. Every sleeve is built from the release ID: 13 styles, 12 palettes. Used sleeves show ring wear — the lower the grade, the more visible.

08

Result

Ready for a backend

The full purchase path works: filters, a stock-aware cart, favourites, search and checkout. It is built with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no libraries; data, state and UI are separated, so connecting an API touches a single layer.

A store you want to stay in.
